correctness.rationale: For each edge, removal separates a tree into sets A and B and the expected reachable component size gain is exactly 2(1-p)F_e(p)/n, with F_e the cross-cut path-length polynomial. Prüfer sequences enumerate every labelled tree up to 8, center-rooted AHU encodings give complete unlabelled representatives, exact edge coefficient vectors permit all-parameter coefficientwise comparisons, and every remaining pair difference factors into one of the five checked forms. The only two forms with roots on (0,1) are p(2p-1) and p(p^2+p-1). An actual execution of the packaged standard-library checker reproduced all 47 unlabelled trees, the exact patterns and both witness vectors. Ten independent rational full-edge-state enumerations checked the basic gain formula. Thus these computations plus the exhaustive algorithm establish the finite sharp theorem; experimental point checks alone are not the proof. Applicability is restricted to n<=8 trees under uniform independent link reliabilities.

originality.rationale: The biological corridor importance objective, pairwise p-distance on trees, and fixed-parameter link optimization are established in the inspected literature. The distinct new finite classification is the exact minimum n=8 for a dispersal-dependent change of the globally optimal single link, the fact that precisely two of 23 eight-vertex unlabelled trees switch, their explicit topologies, and the roots 1/2 and (sqrt(5)-1)/2. Neither an inspected paper nor a retrieved dedicated result contains that sharp all-parameter census. This is an evidence-bounded self-review, not a proof of universal absence.

value.rationale: The established probability-of-connectivity metric is a natural ecological restoration criterion. A sharp minimal example and a complete census of the first eight-vertex exceptions reveal exactly when choosing a corridor according to one assumed dispersal probability can cease to be optimal at another. This finite structural cutoff gives a testable benchmark for habitat restoration optimization and a substantive topology-dependent boundary, unlike an arbitrary numerical instantiation. No implication for heterogeneous real habitats is asserted.
